basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 45.' and it opens '(Vers. 45.) Et vocavit Pharao nomen Joseph Saphaneth Phanee, et dedit ei Aseneth filiam'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 45.) Et vocavit Pharao nomen Joseph Saphaneth Phanee, et dedit ei Aseneth filiam Phutiphar sacerdotis Heliopoleos in uxorem. Licet Hebraice hoc nomen, absconditorum repertorem sonet, tamen quia ab Aegyptio ponitur, ipsius linguae debet habere rationem. Interpretatur ergo sermone Aegyptio SAPHANETH PHANEE (צפנת פענח), sive ut Septuaginta transferre voluerunt, Psomthom-Phanech, Salvator mundi, eo quod orbem terrae ab imminente famis excidio liberavit. Notandum autem, quod Domini quondam et emptoris sui filiam uxorem acceperit, qui ad id locorum pontifex Heliopoleos erat. Neque enim fas absque eunuchis idoli illius esse antistites, ut vera illa Hebraeorum super eo quod ante jam diximus, suspicio comprobetur.
